questions.question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.

options.text: How is your currant brand strategy workinng?
How is your current brrand strategy working?
How is your current brand stretagy working?
How is your current brand strategy working?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 4'.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The** correct sentence** without any spelling errors is:* ''How is your current brand strategy working?'*
 
• In the first sentence, **"currant" **is a type of small, dried fruit and not the correct spelling of **"current,"** meaning 'present or existing at the time.'
 
• Also, "workinng" has an extra 'n,' it should be **"working."**
 
• In the **second sentence,** "brrand" is not correctly spelled. The correct spelling is **"brand.**"
 
• In the **third sentence,** "stretagy" is incorrect. The correct spelling is **"strategy."**
 
• The **fourth sentence,** "How is your current brand strategy working?" is correctly spelled and grammatically correct.

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is:* 'How is your current brand strategy working?'*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

After suffering so many losses, the company is about to go _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1' **i.e. **'Bankrupt'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is: **'Bankrupt'**
 
• **"Bankrupt"** is the correct choice because it refers to the state of being insolvent, or unable to pay debts, which is a common consequence for a company that has suffered many losses.
 
• It's **contextually appropriate** and makes sense given the information in the sentence.

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is: *'After suffering so many losses, the company is about to go **bankrupt.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Silent" **could metaphorically mean the company is closing or ceasing operations, but it's not the most precise term for describing a company's financial state after heavy losses.
 
• **"Cynical"** is an adjective typically used to describe a person's attitude or outlook, not a company's financial state. It's not contextually suitable here.
 
• **"Awry"** means that something is going wrong or is off track. While it could loosely apply to a company in trouble, it doesn't convey the financial distress implied in the sentence as accurately as "bankrupt" does.

select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘no substitution required’, 

The government appears (to be at war with it's own people.)

options.text: to be on war with it's own people

to be at war with its own people

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Mad
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1' **i.e. **'Sound'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate antonym for the word **"Mad"** is: **'Sound'**
 
• **"Mad" **is an adjective which can mean mentally ill or insane, or extremely foolish or angry, depending on the context.
 
• **"Sound"** is used here as an adjective meaning in good condition; not damaged, injured, or diseased.
 
• In a **mental health context**, it is often used to mean mentally healthy or sane, which is the opposite of the mental illness or insanity aspect of "mad."

Therefore, the **correct answer** is:** 'Sound'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** "Indisposition"** is a slight illness or unwillingness, and does not carry a meaning opposite to "mad."
 
• **"Distemper" **is a viral disease of some animals, particularly dogs, or a state of agitation or disorder. It does not represent the opposite of "mad."
 
• **"Dense" **typically means closely compacted in substance or slow to understand. It does not stand as an antonym to "mad."

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Today is cloudy, but yesterday the sun ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3'** i.e. **'Shone'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is: **'Shone'**
 
• **In this sentence, **the verb needed is the past tense of** "shine**," which is **"shone".**
 
• The word **"shone"** refers to emitting or reflecting light, which is what the sun does.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *"Today is cloudy, but yesterday the sun shone."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** "Flamed" **usually refers to producing flames, which is not typically how we describe what the sun does.
 
• **"Shown" **is the past participle of "show," and it does not fit here because it's used when something is being presented or displayed, not when the sun is giving off light.
 
• **"Burned" **can be used to describe the sun's action, but it's not the best fit in this context. "Burned" suggests a harsh, damaging light or heat, which doesn't match with the contrast to a cloudy day being set up in this sentence.

questions.question:

The Gryffindors trooped back up / to the castle, none of them talking; / it have been another long day.

options.text: it have been another long day.
to the castle, none of them talking;

questions.solution:

• The **segment** that contains a grammatical **error** is: *'It have been another long day.'*
 
• The **correct phrase** should be **"it had been another long day."**
 
• The auxiliary verb **"have" **is incorrectly used in this context.
 
• When speaking about something that happened in the past, **"had"** is the **correct auxiliary** verb to use, not **"have".**

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* "The Gryffindors trooped back up to the castle, none of them talking; it had been another long day*."

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it. select “no substitution required’.

He suggested (there was collusions through objectors, due to similarities) in some letters sent to the council.

options.text: there was collusions from the objector, due to similarities
there was collusion between objectors, due to similarities
their was collusion by the objectors, due to similarities

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** most appropriate option** to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence is:* 'There was collusion between objectors, due to similarities'*
 
• The phrase* "there was collusions through objectors, due to similarities"* is **incorrect.**
 
• The word **"collusions" should be "collusion,"** which is a noun that does not have a plural form.
 
• Additionally, the preposition **"through" **is inappropriate in this context.
 
• **When speaking about **collusion, which implies a secret or illicit cooperation, "between" is the correct preposition to use, indicating the mutual involvement of the parties.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* "He suggested there was collusion between objectors, due to similarities in some letters sent to the council."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** "There was collusions from the objector, due to similarities"** is incorrect because "collusions" is not the right form of the word, and the preposition "from" doesn't appropriately convey the mutual involvement in collusion.
 
• **"Their was collusion by the objectors, due to similarities"** is grammatically incorrect. The correct spelling for the context would be "there" not "their", and "by the objectors" doesn't capture the mutual nature of collusion as effectively as "between objectors."

questions.question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

The story of human evolution _____ a moving target in recent years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 2'** i.e**. 'Has been'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct alternative to fill in the blank is: **'Has been'.**
 
• The verb that fits the context of this sentence is **"has been."**
 
• **In this case**, the present perfect tense **"has been"** is used to describe a situation or state that began in the past and continues to the present time, which fits the context of "the story of human evolution."

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: '*The story of human evolution has been a moving target in recent years.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Had being"** is grammatically incorrect in English.** "Had been"** could be used in a different context, but it refers to a state or situation that was in existence in the past and is no longer in existence now, which doesn't suit this context.
 
• **"Have been"** is incorrect because the subject "The story of human evolution" is singular, so the singular form "has" should be used, not the plural "have."
 
• **"Did has"** is not correct English grammar. It mixes past simple ("did") with present perfect ("has"), which is not allowed.

questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct,

__
 
• The** correct answer** is: **'No improvement'**

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* 'My grandmother taught me how to sew my own clothes.'*

• **"Taught I" **is incorrect because** "I" **is a subject pronoun and should not be used as an object. The correct object pronoun, as used in the original sentence, is "me."

questions.question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error’.

Our passage across the Arabian Sea/ was smooth as the most timid of/ navigators could desire.

options.text: Our passage across the Arabian Sea
was smooth as the most timid of

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: **was smooth as the most timid of**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ‘As’ is used to denote equality. It is used when a sentence contains **adjectives **in the positive and comparative forms.
 
• It is used in this manner: as ______ as. The blank should be an adjective.
 
 
• Example: She is** as good as**, if not better than her brother.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in the given question, "as...as" is being used in a slightly more complex way to compare the smoothness of the passage to the level of smoothness that the most timid of navigators could desire.
 
• This is a figurative comparison, expressing that the passage was extremely smooth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *Our passage across the Arabian Sea was **as **smooth as the most timid of navigators could desire.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• Remember, **NOT** all adjectives can be used in the structure "as + adjective + as".
 
• It's typically used with gradable adjectives — adjectives that can have different degrees or levels.
 
• For instance, words like 'happy', 'excited', 'sad', 'good', 'bad', 'smooth' etc., can be used, but non-gradable adjectives like 'dead', 'perfect', 'unique' typically are not used in this structure.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1'** i.e**. 'Wrote'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 1 is: **'Wrote'.**
 
• Given the context of the sentence, we are talking about a past event that occurred in 700 BCE.
 
• The correct past tense of the verb **"write"** is **"wrote."**
 
• **It fits perfectly** into the sentence's historical context, which refers to something the Greek poet Hesiod did in the past.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'In 700 BCE Greek post Hesiod** wrote** “Theogony” and “Work and Days”. In these mythologies, Atlas was a Titan (2) ______ enormous strength. He along with other titans (3) ______ the gods of Mount Olympus. While the other Titans were banished to Tartarus after being defeated by the god Zeus as retribution, Atlas (4) _______ was forced to carry the earth and the sky for an eternity. In depictions of Atlas. obviously carved by human based on myths, he is shown as a stooped figure carrying the (5) _____ on his shoulders. Because of his association with the globe. maps began to be decorated with this image of Atlas. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's briefly look at the other options:
 
 
• **"Had written" **is the past perfect tense and is used when we want to show that one past action happened before another past action. This isn't needed in this context.
 
• **"Will write"** is future tense, and it's not suitable here because we're discussing a past event.
 
• **"Writes"** is present tense, which is also not appropriate here as we're referring to an event in the past.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3' **i.e. **'Of'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 2 is: **'Of'.**
 
• **In this sentence, **we are trying to describe Atlas as a Titan possessing or characterized by "enormous strength."
 
• When denoting possession or characteristic, we use **"of."**

Therefore, the** correct sentence **is: *'In 700 BCE Greek post Hesiod wrote “Theogony” and “Work and Days”. In these mythologies, Atlas was a Titan **of** enormous strength. He along with other titans (3) ______ the gods of Mount Olympus. While the other Titans were banished to Tartarus after being defeated by the god Zeus as retribution, Atlas (4) _______ was forced to carry the earth and the sky for an eternity. In depictions of Atlas. obviously carved by human based on myths, he is shown as a stooped figure carrying the (5) _____ on his shoulders. Because of his association with the globe. maps began to be decorated with this image of Atlas. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's briefly look at the other options:
 
 
• **"From" **generally denotes origin, source, or starting point. It would not be correct in this context.
 
• **"In"** typically refers to a location or a state of being, and it is not appropriate here.
 
• **"At" **often denotes a specific position or place, which doesn't fit with the concept of possessing strength.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3'** i.e. **'Challenged'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 3 is:** 'Challenged'**
 
• **In the context **of this sentence, the Titans, including Atlas, are opposing the gods of Mount Olympus.
 
• The most suitable word that describes this opposition or confrontation is **"challenged."**

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'In 700 BCE Greek post Hesiod wrote “Theogony” and “Work and Days”. In these mythologies, Atlas was a Titan of enormous strength. He along with other titans **challenged **the gods of Mount Olympus. While the other Titans were banished to Tartarus after being defeated by the god Zeus as retribution, Atlas (4) _______ was forced to carry the earth and the sky for an eternity. In depictions of Atlas. obviously carved by human based on myths, he is shown as a stooped figure carrying the (5) _____ on his shoulders. Because of his association with the globe. maps began to be decorated with this image of Atlas. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's briefly look at the other options:
 
 
• **"Collaborated" **implies working together, which doesn't fit here because the Titans and the gods of Mount Olympus were not on the same side.
 
• **"Claimed" **is used when asserting or stating something, often without providing evidence or proof. This isn't appropriate in this context as the Titans were not asserting anything; they were opposing the gods.
 
• **"Corroborated"** means to confirm or give support to (a statement, theory, or finding), which also does not fit the context as the Titans were not supporting or confirming anything related to the gods.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'** i.e. **'however'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 4 is: **'However'.**
 
• The word** "however" **is used to introduce a statement that contrasts with or seems to contradict something that has been said previously.
 
• **In this context,** the Titans were banished to Tartarus after their defeat, but Atlas faced a different punishment.
 
• The word **"however"** effectively captures this contrast.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'In 700 BCE Greek post Hesiod wrote “Theogony” and “Work and Days”. In these mythologies, Atlas was a Titan of enormous strength. He along with other titans challenged the gods of Mount Olympus. While the other Titans were banished to Tartarus after being defeated by the god Zeus as retribution, Atlas **however **was forced to carry the earth and the sky for an eternity. In depictions of Atlas. obviously carved by human based on myths, he is shown as a stooped figure carrying the (5) _____ on his shoulders. Because of his association with the globe. maps began to be decorated with this image of Atlas. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's briefly look at the other options:
 
 
• **"Despite"** implies that something happened or is true even though there were things that might prevent it. Here, it wouldn't accurately capture the contrasting fate of Atlas versus the other Titans.
 
• **"In fact"** is used to emphasize the truth of an assertion, especially one contrary to what might have been expected or what has been stated. This doesn't fit the context here because we're not emphasizing the truth of an assertion but stating a contrast.
 
• **"Unlike"** is used to emphasize the difference of something in comparison with another thing. But in this context, we need a word to mark the contrast between the general fate of the Titans and the specific fate of Atlas, which makes "however" more suitable.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 2'** i.e. **'Globe'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in **blank No. 5 **is: **'Globe'.**
 
• **Atlas,** according to Greek mythology, was punished by being forced to hold up the sky.
 
• However, in art and literature, this is often depicted as Atlas carrying the entire world or globe on his shoulders.
 
• Thus, **"globe"** is the most suitable word to use here.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'In 700 BCE Greek post Hesiod wrote “Theogony” and “Work and Days”. In these mythologies, Atlas was a Titan of enormous strength. He along with other titans challenged the gods of Mount Olympus. While the other Titans were banished to Tartarus after being defeated by the god Zeus as retribution, Atlas however was forced to carry the earth and the sky for an eternity. In depictions of Atlas. obviously carved by human based on myths, he is shown as a stooped figure carrying the **globe **on his shoulders. Because of his association with the globe. maps began to be decorated with this image of Atlas. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's briefly look at the other options:
 
 
• **"Universe"** refers to all existing matter, energy, and space considered as a whole. It is too broad for the specific punishment of Atlas, which was carrying the Earth (or the "globe").
 
• **"Seas"** would not be correct because Atlas was not tasked with holding the seas. His task was holding up the sky or the Earth.
 
• **"Heavens"** could potentially work, as Atlas was tasked with holding up the sky (often referred to as the "heavens" in older texts). However, due to the later sentence mentioning his association with the globe and maps, "globe" makes more sense in this context.
